findings.title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this reports 2 pages instead of 1, and for 100/50 it reports 3 instead of 2. Because showingLast compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the Next control stays enabled on the real last page and navigates to an empty phantom page. The formula should be a ceiling division (with the zero-count case handled separately).

findings.title: Group creation silently discards the alias_level chosen in the UI
findings.body: The client's Group#asJSON sends alias_level (along with name and visible) on POST /admin/groups, and the admin form renders the alias-level selector for new groups, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. A group created with e.g. alias_level 'everyone' is therefore saved with the column default (0/nobody) with no error, and the admin must edit the group again to set the intended mentioning permissions.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and invalid limit/offset parameters
findings.body: limit and offset are taken directly from params with only to_i coercion. A caller can pass limit=1000000 to force the server to load and serialize every member of a very large (e.g. automatic) group in a single request, defeating the new pagination and causing heavy memory/response load; negative values (limit=-1, offset=-5) are passed to ActiveRecord/Postgres and can raise a 500 error. Both values need clamping to a sane range (e.g. limit within 1..some maximum, offset >= 0).

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member (the companion success example on line 125 correctly uses :delete). Controller specs dispatch by action name rather than through the router, so this test passes even though the verb it documents does not exist; it would not catch a routing/verb mismatch and misdocuments the API contract. It should use :delete like the success case.
